title: The Control Room Inside Your Head

pages.text: The Control Room Inside Your Head: A Story About the Brain

‘My brain?’ Milo asked. Dr. Chen nodded. ‘Your brain is like the control room inside your head.’ Zara touched her forehead. ‘So my brain tells my body to move?’ ‘Yes,’ said Dr. Chen. ‘When you decide to run, your brain sends messages through your spinal cord and nerves. Those messages travel to your muscles.’ Milo looked amazed. ‘Like tiny signals?’ ‘Exactly,’ said Dr. Chen. ‘Your nerves carry messages very quickly.’

Zara pointed to her eyes. ‘What about seeing?’ ‘Your eyes collect information,’ Dr. Chen said. ‘Then your brain helps you understand what you see.’ Milo held up the ball. ‘So my eyes saw the ball, and my brain helped me catch it?’ ‘That’s right,’ said Dr. Chen. Brain Clue Your senses gather information. Then your brain helps you understand what you see, hear, and feel.

Later in class, Dr. Chen drew a simple brain on the board. ‘Different parts of the brain have different jobs,’ she explained. ‘Some parts help you think. Some help you remember. Some help you move. Some help you balance.’ Zara raised her hand. ‘What about feelings?’ Brain Clue Different parts of the brain help with thinking, memory, movement, and balance.

'The brain helps with feelings too,' Dr. Chen said. 'It helps you feel happy, worried, excited, calm, or curious.' Milo grinned. 'So my brain is doing homework, sports, memories, and feelings?' 'All day long,' said Dr. Chen. Brain Clue Your brain helps control emotions as well as learning, memories, and movement.

Zara looked surprised. ‘Even when I’m sleeping?’ ‘Yes,’ Dr. Chen said. ‘Your brain still works while you sleep. It helps your body rest, stores memories, and keeps important body jobs going.’ Milo took a deep breath. ‘Like breathing?’ ‘Yes,’ said Dr. Chen. ‘Your brain helps control breathing, heartbeat, and many things you do not even have to think about.’ Brain Clue Your brain keeps working while you sleep. It helps control breathing, heartbeat, and memory.

Zara looked at Milo. ‘So the brain is not just for thinking.’ ‘It is for running the whole body,’ Milo said. That afternoon, Zara drew a picture of a control room in her notebook. Inside it, tiny workers sent messages to the eyes, ears, hands, feet, heart, and lungs. At the bottom she wrote: ‘My brain is the boss, the messenger, the memory keeper, and the problem solver.’ Brain Clue The brain works like a control room. It sends messages all around the body.

The brain is the body’s control center. It sends messages through the spinal cord and nerves. It helps with movement, thinking, memory, senses, balance, emotions, breathing, and heartbeat. The brain works all day and even keeps working while we sleep.
